answer_text:
Let

\[
A=\int_0^1 t f(t)\,dt, \qquad B=\int_0^1 t^2 f(t)\,dt.
\]

Then the integral term in the equation becomes

\[
\int_0^1 t(x+t)f(t)\,dt
= x\int_0^1 t f(t)\,dt+\int_0^1 t^2 f(t)\,dt
= xA+B.
\]

So the given equation implies

\[
f(x)=x+xA+B=(1+A)x+B.
\]

Now compute \(A\) and \(B\) using this form of \(f\):

\[
A=\int_0^1 t f(t)\,dt
=\int_0^1 t\bigl((1+A)t+B\bigr)\,dt
=\frac{1+A}{3}+\frac{B}{2}.
\]

Also,

\[
B=\int_0^1 t^2 f(t)\,dt
=\int_0^1 t^2\bigl((1+A)t+B\bigr)\,dt
=\frac{1+A}{4}+\frac{B}{3}.
\]

From the equation for \(B\),

\[
B-\frac{B}{3}=\frac{1+A}{4}
\]

so

\[
\frac{2B}{3}=\frac{1+A}{4}
\]

and therefore

\[
B=\frac{3(1+A)}{8}.
\]

Substitute this into the equation for \(A\):

\[
A=\frac{1+A}{3}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{3(1+A)}{8}
\]

\[
A=\frac{1+A}{3}+\frac{3(1+A)}{16}
\]

\[
A=\frac{25(1+A)}{48}.
\]

Thus

\[
48A=25+25A
\]

\[
23A=25
\]

\[
A=\frac{25}{23}.
\]

Then

\[
B=\frac{3(1+A)}{8}
=\frac{3}{8}\left(1+\frac{25}{23}\right)
=\frac{3}{8}\cdot \frac{48}{23}
=\frac{18}{23}.
\]

Now

\[
\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx
=\int_0^1 \bigl((1+A)x+B\bigr)\,dx
=\frac{1+A}{2}+B.
\]

Substitute \(A=\frac{25}{23}\) and \(B=\frac{18}{23}\):

\[
\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx
=\frac{1}{2}\left(1+\frac{25}{23}\right)+\frac{18}{23}
=\frac{24}{23}+\frac{18}{23}
=\frac{42}{23}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{42}{23}}
\]
